title: Impersonation during account registration
description: An attacker could impersonate the Homeowner during the account registration process, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the Home Hub system and enrolling cameras/sensors under false pretenses.
assumptions: The registration process relies on credentials that can be compromised or forged.

title: Disclosure of personal information during registration
description: Sensitive personal information provided by the Homeowner during account registration (e.g., name, address, contact details) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: The registration process collects PII that must be transmitted to the Home Hub.

title: Linkability of homeowner activities across devices
description: The Homeowner's registration and camera/sensor enrollment activities could be linked across multiple devices or sessions, potentially enabling profiling of the homeowner's behavior patterns and home security setup.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains logs or records that could be correlated with other data sources.

title: Linkability of Guest Access Events
description: An observer could link this guest's door access event to other activities or identify patterns in guest usage, potentially revealing behavioral information about the guest user.
assumptions: Observer has visibility of the access event and can correlate it with other data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability at flow level

title: Detection of Guest User Access
description: An observer could detect that a guest user is accessing the home system by observing the door unlock event, system response, or communication flows, revealing the guest's presence and participation.
assumptions: Observer can observe system responses or door unlock events
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 chosen based on context about detecting threats through observed communication and system responses

title: Disclosure of Access Code
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could be observed or intercepted by others, leading to unauthorized access or code disclosure.
assumptions: Access code is entered in a way that could be observed (e.g., keypad, screen)
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 selected for data disclosure at flow level; code interception is a realistic concern

title: Usurpation of Guest Access
description: An unauthorized party could observe or intercept the access code and use it to gain entry, usurping the guest's legitimate access rights.
assumptions: Access code is observable or interceptable; no authentication beyond the code
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 for usurpation at flow level; code-based access is inherently vulnerable to interception

title: Linkability of sensor events to individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local event log can be linked to specific individuals based on timing, location patterns, and event types, revealing occupancy patterns and presence in the home.
assumptions: Events contain sufficient contextual information (timestamps, sensor locations) to correlate with specific individuals.

title: Identification of individuals from event data
description: Door events and motion sensor data can identify who entered/exited the home, when they were present, and their movement patterns within the residence.
assumptions: Event data includes sufficient detail (e.g., door names, sensor locations) to identify specific individuals.

title: Unauthorized access to local event log
description: The local event log storing sensitive occupancy and access data may be accessible to unauthorized individuals (e.g., other household members, visitors, or through device compromise).
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected or access controls are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Assumes local log has some level of access control; severity depends on actual protection measures.

title: Unauthorized use of event data for surveillance
description: Event data in the local log could be used for unauthorized surveillance purposes, such as monitoring household member behavior, tracking movement patterns, or inferring activities.
assumptions: Event data is accessible and could be repurposed for surveillance without consent.
uncertainty_note: Depends on who has access to the local log and their intentions.

title: Identifiability of video footage in cloud storage
description: Cloud video storage (DS2) contains recorded camera clips that can be linked to specific individuals, locations, and activities. Unauthorized access to this data could reveal personal information about household members and their daily routines.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability at data store level

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video footage
description: Cloud video storage (DS2) may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, data breaches, or improper access controls, leading to disclosure of sensitive video footage to unauthorized parties. This could result in privacy violations and potential misuse of personal video data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for disclosure at data store level

title: Linkability of video clips across time and context
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage (DS2) can be linked across different time periods, locations, or events, potentially creating comprehensive profiles of household activities and behaviors. This linkability could enable surveillance and tracking beyond the intended scope.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability at data store level

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub (P1) forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend (P2), potentially disclosing personal data beyond minimal requirements. Motion data may contain location patterns or behavioral information that exceeds what's strictly necessary for the alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion data contains personal information; the disclosure to P2 is not limited to what's minimally required for the alert function.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure of personal data to involved parties. The exact nature of 'motion alert' data and whether it contains PII is inferred from typical smart home contexts.

title: Unauthorized interception of motion alerts
description: Real-time motion alert data transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to potential privacy violations.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1 is inferred based on standard LINDDUN usurpation patterns for Process→Process flows. Encryption status of this flow is not specified in the context.

title: Notification interception during transmission
description: Motion-detected notification could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission from mobile app backend to homeowner's phone, potentially exposing homeowner's location and activity patterns.
assumptions: Network transmission is not fully encrypted or authentication is insufficient
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard mobile app security practices apply

title: Linkability of motion events to homeowner behavior patterns
description: Motion-detected notifications could be linked with other data about the homeowner (e.g., access logs, other notifications) to infer behavior patterns, presence/absence, or routine activities.
assumptions: Other data flows exist that could be correlated with this notification
uncertainty_note: Depends on what other data flows exist in the system

title: Excessive data in motion notification
description: Notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., exact location coordinates, precise timestamp, type of motion) when a simple alert would suffice.
assumptions: Notification includes detailed metadata beyond basic alert
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification payload design

title: Unauthorized access to homeowner notification
description: If homeowner's device is compromised or authentication is weak, unauthorized parties could access motion-detected notifications, revealing when homeowner is home or away.
assumptions: Homeowner device authentication or notification access controls are insufficient
uncertainty_note: Depends on device security posture and authentication mechanisms

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor may contain residual identifiers or patterns that could be linked with other datasets to re-identify individual users
assumptions: Vendor may have access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the analytics
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as it's a common node for linkability threats in data sharing scenarios

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Analytics Data
description: Cloud analytics vendor may disclose the aggregated device-usage data to unauthorized third parties or use it for purposes beyond the agreed scope
assumptions: Vendor may have weak access controls or may share data with business partners without proper authorization
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node for Process->ExternalEntity flows

title: Identification Through Aggregated Data Analysis
description: Even aggregated analytics data may be susceptible to statistical inference attacks that could identify individual users through pattern analysis
assumptions: Large-scale analytics data can be analyzed using sophisticated statistical methods to de-anonymize users
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 applies to identification risks even in aggregated data contexts

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Processing
description: Cloud analytics vendor may process the shared analytics data in violation of applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.)
assumptions: Vendor may not have adequate privacy compliance frameworks or may process data beyond the scope of consent
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is appropriate for external entity compliance risks in data sharing flows

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data during retrieval
description: The mobile app backend (P2) retrieves video data from cloud storage (DS2) for playback. If the retrieval mechanism lacks proper access controls or authentication, video data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or leaked through the backend interface.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree.

title: Video content reveals identifiable information about homeowner
description: Video clips inherently contain visual data that can identify individuals (the homeowner and potentially others). When retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend, this identifiable information could be exposed or misused.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree.

title: Unauthorized access to video playback by non-homeowner
description: If authentication or authorization controls are insufficient at the mobile app backend (P2), unauthorized users could access and view video content that should only be accessible to the homeowner.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle for video data
description: Video data retrieved from cloud storage (DS2) may be retained longer than necessary at the mobile app backend (P2), violating the storage limitation principle. Video data is particularly sensitive and should be minimized and deleted when no longer needed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1.4 was provided in context and applies to storage limitation concerns.
